newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour says will set "sensible" minimum wage.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour says will set "sensible" minimum wage.

text.p: Britain's Labour Party said on Thursday it would introduce a "sensibly set" minimum wage but denied it would roll back reams of union legislation passed in the 1980s.

"Introduced sensibly, the minimum wage will remove the worst excesses of low pay while cutting some of the massive four billion stg benefits bill by which the taxpayer subsidises companies that pay very low wages," Labour's election manifesto said.
It said every modern industrial country has a minimum wage, including the United States and Japan.
The manifesto also said the key elements of trade union legislation introduced in the 1980s would remain. They include laws on balloting for industrial action, picketing and striking.

"There must be minimum standards for the individual at work, including a minimum wage within a flexible labour market," it said. "We need a sensible balance in industrial relations law -- rights and duties go together."
Last week, the ruling Conservatives opened their most successful campaign front to date, accusing Labour of still being in thrall to their old union allies.
Prime Minister John Major said a Labour government could lead to the return of "overmighty" trade unions that would threaten Britain's economic prosperity.
Labour has also promised to sign the European Union Social Chapter, which guarantees minimum employment rights. The Conservative government has refused to sign up.
Elections are set for May 1 and Labour, riding high in the opinion polls, is poised to take power for the first time since 1979.
